*Quantum of Solace* was released on DVD and [Blu-ray](/wiki/Blu-ray "Blu-ray") by [MGM Home Entertainment](/wiki/MGM_Home_Entertainment "MGM Home Entertainment") via [20th Century Fox Home Entertainment](/wiki/20th_Century_Fox_Home_Entertainment "20th Century Fox Home Entertainment") in Australia, the United Kingdom and North America from 18 to 24 March 2009. On the DVD sales chart the film opened at No. 3, grossing $21,894,957 from 1.21 million DVD units sold.[[134]](#cite_note-the-numbers1-135) As of 1 November 2009, 2,643,250 DVD units were sold, generating $44,110,750 in sales revenue.[[134]](#cite_note-the-numbers1-135) These figures do not include Blu-ray sales or DVD rentals. The DVDs were released in both a standard one-disc set and a deluxe two-disc special edition. There are no audio commentaries or deleted scenes on these editions.[[135]](#cite_note-136) An [Ultra HD Blu-ray](/wiki/Ultra_HD_Blu-ray "Ultra HD Blu-ray") release was released on October 22, 2019.

The **Western Front** was a [military theatre](/wiki/European_theatre_of_World_War_II "European theatre of World War II") of [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") encompassing [Denmark](/wiki/Denmark "Denmark"), [Norway](/wiki/Norway "Norway"), [Luxembourg](/wiki/Luxembourg "Luxembourg"), [Belgium](/wiki/Belgium "Belgium"), the [Netherlands](/wiki/Netherlands "Netherlands"), the [United Kingdom](/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), [France](/wiki/French_Third_Republic "French Third Republic"), and [Germany](/wiki/Nazi_Germany "Nazi Germany"). The [Italian front](/wiki/Italian_campaign_(World_War_II) "Italian campaign (World War II)") is considered a separate but related theatre.[[k]](#cite_note-49) The Western Front's 1944–1945 phase was officially deemed the [European Theater](/wiki/European_Theater_of_Operations,_United_States_Army "European Theater of Operations, United States Army") by the United States, whereas Italy fell under the [Mediterranean Theater](/wiki/Mediterranean_Theater_of_Operations,_United_States_Army "Mediterranean Theater of Operations, United States Army") along with the [North African campaign](/wiki/North_African_campaign "North African campaign"). The Western Front was marked by two phases of large-scale combat operations. The first phase saw the capitulation of Luxembourg, Netherlands, Belgium, and France during May and June 1940 after their defeat in the [Low Countries](/wiki/Low_Countries "Low Countries") and the northern half of France, and continued into an air war between Germany and Britain that climaxed with the [Battle of Britain](/wiki/Battle_of_Britain "Battle of Britain"). The second phase consisted of large-scale ground combat (supported by [a massive strategic air war](/wiki/Defence_of_the_Reich "Defence of the Reich") considered to be an additional front), which began in June 1944 with the [Allied landings in Normandy](/wiki/Normandy_landings "Normandy landings") and continued until the [defeat of Germany](/wiki/Victory_in_Europe_Day "Victory in Europe Day") in May 1945 with its [invasion](/wiki/Western_Allied_invasion_of_Germany "Western Allied invasion

Honolulu experiences a [hot semi-arid climate](/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") ([Köppen classification](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_classification "Köppen classification") *BSh*), with a mostly dry summer season, due to a [rain shadow](/wiki/Rain_shadow "Rain shadow") effect.[[33]](#cite_note-34) Despite temperatures that meet the tropical threshold of all months having a mean temperature of 64.4 °F (18.0 °C) or higher, the city receives too little precipitation to be classified as tropical.

Temperatures vary little throughout the year, with average high temperatures of 80–90 °F (27–32 °C) and average lows of 65–75 °F (18–24 °C). Nevertheless, there are slight seasons. The "winter" months from December to March can occasionally see lows fall below 67 °F (19 °C), whereas the "summer" from June to September can get a limited number of hot days achieving 90 °F (32 °C) or higher. This occurs on an average of only 32 days annually,[[34]](#cite_note-NOAA-35)[[b]](#cite_note-36) with lows in the upper 50s °F (14–15 °C) once or twice a year. The highest recorded temperature was 95 °F (35 °C) on September 19, 1994, and August 31, 2019.[[34]](#cite_note-NOAA-35) The lowest recorded temperature was 52 °F (11 °C) on February 16, 1902, and January 20, 1969.[[34]](#cite_note-NOAA-35)

The annual average rainfall is 16.41 inches (417 millimeters),[[34]](#cite_note-NOAA-35) which mainly occurs from October through early April, with very little rainfall in the summer. However, both seasons experience a similar number of rainy days. Light showers occur in summer, while heavier rain falls during winter. Honolulu has an average of 278 sunny days and 89.2 rainy days per year.

Although the city is in the tropics, [hurricanes](/wiki/Hurricane "Hurricane") are quite rare. The last recorded hurricane that hit near Honolulu was Category 4 [Hurricane Iniki](/wiki/Hurricane_Iniki "Hurricane Iniki") in 1992. [Tornadoes](/wiki/Tornado "Tornado") are also uncommon and occur about every 15 years. Due to their intelligence, obedient nature, athleticism and looks poodles were frequently employed in circuses, particularly in France.[[2]](#cite_note-Alderton-08-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5)[[7]](#cite_note-Fiorone-7) In French circuses poodles were selectively bred down in size to create what is now known as the miniature poodle, which was known as the toy poodle until 1907, as a smaller sized dog is easier to handle and transport in a travelling circus.[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5) As circus performers the variety was frequently seen performing all manner of tricks including walking tightropes, acting out comedies and even performing magic and card tricks.[[2]](#cite_note-Alderton-08-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5)

The Toy Poodle was created at the beginning of the 20th century when breeders again bred Miniature Poodles down in size to create a popular companion dog.[[2]](#cite_note-Alderton-08-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5) Initially, these efforts resulted in disfigured or misshapen pups, as well as pups with behavioural problems, as a result of irresponsible breeding for dwarfed size only. As new breeding practices were adopted, the variety became set as a toy-sized replica of the original.[[2]](#cite_note-Alderton-08-2)[[3]](#cite_note-Fogle-3)[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5) Later attempts to create an even smaller variety, the Teacup Poodle, were unable to overcome serious genetic abnormalities and were abandoned.[[5]](#cite_note-Morris-5)

The last of the Poodle varieties to be recognised was the Medium Poodle, which in size is mid way in between the Standard and the Miniature Poodle.
